content_html: # Cancelling "Hey" If you don't know, "Hey" is a somewhat popular email client, created by industry legend DHH. I found Hey to work really well for me and really liked it. It costs $99/year, and I've been a loyal customer for four years, meaning I've given them $396 in total. I found out today that 1. They apparently also have a blog publishing platform. 2. DHH used it to write post a post titled [Wolves, sheep, and gypsies](https://world.hey.com/dhh/wolves-sheep-and-gypsies-ba44af6a). Here is a quote from it: > Whether it's wolves or gypsies, you can't just let the problems get out of hand. You have to act. You have to protect the sheep. Standing idly by while your livestock is devoured by predators or your neighborhood is taken over by migrants is a pathetic abdication of any functioning society's most basic duty to its citizens. > > When wolves get out of control, you shoot them. When gypsies take over public spaces, you deport them. This isn't hard, it isn't cruel. It's the basic logic of self-preservation. I'm a big believer in live-and-let-live. That's why I don't have bad feelings towards DHH. I definitely don't believe in trying to change people's minds by shouting at them or shaming them. I think that the impulse to shout and shame comes from "[conflict theory](https://slatestarcodex.com/2018/01/24/conflict-vs-mistake/)," which says that when two people have a political disagreement, it usually stems from a conflict in their values or interests that can never be resolved amicably. I believe in mistake theory, which says that when two people have a political disagreement, it's likely that they both have shared intentions but one of them is just wrong on the facts. And I don't see any point in cutting someone off who's wrong on the facts, as that only robs me of the ability to change their mind. But there is still a line. I'll be your friend, but I don't need to be your business partner. ---- Paul Graham [said this](https://paulgraham.com/say.html): > If a statement is false, that's the worst thing you can say about it. You don't need to say that it's heretical. I love this quote. Focusing on what's actually true and false in real life, and rather than the associations and ramifications of the statements we perceive our perceived opponents making, is the only way that we can rectify our mistakes. However, I have to say that the statement "If a statement is false, that's the worst thing you can say about it" is in fact false. For example, if I give someone inaccurate medical advice, that is not only false, it is false and harmful. And "false and harmful" is worse than "false". I think, if I had to modify Paul Graham's statement, I'd say: > A false statement can only cause harm if it is believed. So to stop the statement's harm, convince people that it's false. I'm not super happy with the wording, but whatever. So, which statement of DHH's is false? --- DHH says: > When wolves get out of control, you shoot them. When gypsies take over public spaces, you deport them. Wolves are all predators. There are no "good wolves" (from the perspective of a sheep.) So if wolves are out of control, it can make sense to systematically shoot them. However, in any ethnicity of people, there will be some who are good and some who are bad. This makes people very unlike wolves. Because some are good and some are bad, the best solution is to have an apparatus that detects the bad ones and deals with them in some way, such as deporting or imprisoning or fining them. It is not fair to punish them collectively for the crimes committed by only some of them. You do not need to deport all of them to deport the ones who "take over public spaces". Aside from fairness, are there other reasons to support individuated enforcement? I think so. Because almost all of the people involved are EU citizens, they cannot be deported without cause. Any kind of mass deportation plan would have to change that, which would be legally tricky to say the least. However, enforcing the existing laws requires no legal action, and could start tomorrow if the relevant executive wanted it to. DHH might say "well, individuated enforcement sounds nice, but we don't seem to have the will to enforce our laws anymore." Well, my understanding of Denmark is that they also don't have the will to start doing mass deportations of EU citizens, and DHH is advocating to change that. Why not advocate for individuated enforcement, seeing as it's the easier and fairer option? --- ## The Missing Mood Bryan Caplan has blogged about "[The Missing Moods](https://www.econlib.org/archives/2016/01/the_invisible_t.html)". He says: > You can learn a lot by comparing the mood reasonable proponents _would_ hold to the mood actual proponents _do_ hold. I think this concept is very instructive. He gives an example of a common "missing mood": > Modern warfare almost always leads to killing lots of innocents; if governments were held to the same standards as individuals, these killings would be manslaughter, if not murder.  This doesn’t mean that war is never justified.  But the [reasonable hawkish mood](http://www.econlib.org/archives/2010/07/the_conservativ.html) is sorrow – and constant yearning for a peaceful path.  The kind of emotions that flow out of, “We are in a tragic situation.  After painstaking research on all the available options, we regretfully conclude that we have to kill many thousands of innocent civilians in order to avoid even greater evils.  This is true even after adjusting for the inaccuracy of our past predictions about foreign policy.” > > I have never personally known a hawk who expresses such moods, and know of none in the public eye.  Instead, the standard hawk moods are anger and machismo.  Ted Cruz’s [recent quip](http://www.bloomberg.com/politics/articles/2015-12-06/cruz-gaining-on-trump-in-iowa-intensifies-war-rhetoric), “I don’t know if sand can glow in the dark, but we’re going to find out” is typical. I think it's a good point. War is often a terrible thing for civilians. If initiating a war is truly necessary, then that's what you have to do, but it's odd to be happy about it. And if you're happy about it, it gives others reason not to trust your reasoning. The same kind of applies here. I think that the reasonable mood might be closer to "Romani people are simply causing more problems than our police force is equipped to handle right now. We have exhausted other options and for now the best option is to prevent new migration of Roma people into Denmark and gradually deport the ones we have. It's terrible that some innocent people who would have contributed to Denmark will be caught in the crossfire simply for being Romani, but there's simply no alternative." But that's not the mood I got from the piece. That sentiment contains a factual error, that "there's simply no alternative". As I mentioned earlier, the alternative is individuated enforcement. But my point is that it's possible to want what DHH wants while trying to treat everyone with dignity, and simply acknowledging an unfortunate reality where deportation of some innocent people is simply the best option. The fact that he isn't doing that suggests to me that there's a more fundamental mistake in his reasoning. Notice that in DHH's entire article, there's not a single sentence acknowledging that the category of "gypsy" contains uninvolved people contributing positively to Denmark. I'd argue that every part of the post does the opposite. You should read the post to see for yourself, but it starts with a long section about the growing threat of wolves in Denmark. As I mentioned earlier, every wolf is a predator and a threat, and in Denmark according to DHH they are reproducing rapidly. Immediately after, we have "Cue the gypsies in Copenhagen, and their increasingly brazen behavior". There's no indication that there's any possibility that a single one could by innocent or worthy of respect, any more than there's an indication that a single wolf could be. Let's try to compare numerator to denominator. The "increasingly brazen behavior" that DHH constitutes "gypsies take\[ing] over public spaces", that must be stopped by "the basic logic of self-preservation," is one illegal tent camp. I'd guess this constitutes tens of people. Meanwhile, there are thousands of Roma living in Denmark. ------ Sunday, July 28, 2026

sentences.zh: 然而，我不得不说，“如果一个陈述是错误的，那就是你能说的最糟糕的事情”这句话实际上是错误的。

sentences.zh: 例如，如果我给某人提供不准确的医疗建议，那不仅是错误的，而且是错误的和有害的。

sentences.en: And "false and harmful" is worse than "false".
sentences.zh: 而“虚假有害”比“虚假”更糟糕。

sentences.en: I think, if I had to modify Paul Graham's statement, I'd say: > A false statement can only cause harm if it is believed.
sentences.zh: 我想，如果我必须修改保罗·格雷厄姆的说法，我会说： > 错误的陈述只有在被相信的情况下才会造成伤害。

sentences.en: So to stop the statement's harm, convince people that it's false.
sentences.zh: 因此，要阻止该声明的危害，请让人们相信它是错误的。

sentences.en: I'm not super happy with the wording, but whatever.
sentences.zh: 我对措辞不太满意，但无论如何。

sentences.en: So, which statement of DHH's is false? --- DHH says: > When wolves get out of control, you shoot them.
sentences.zh: 那么，DHH的哪项声明是错误的？ --- DHH 说： > 当狼失去控制时，你就射杀它们。

sentences.en: When gypsies take over public spaces, you deport them.
sentences.zh: 当吉普赛人占领公共场所时，你就将他们驱逐出境。

sentences.en: Wolves are all predators.
sentences.zh: 狼都是掠食者。

sentences.en: There are no "good wolves" (from the perspective of a sheep.)
sentences.zh: 没有“好狼”（从羊的角度来看。）

sentences.en: So if wolves are out of control, it can make sense to systematically shoot them.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果狼失去控制，有系统地射杀它们是有意义的。

sentences.en: However, in any ethnicity of people, there will be some who are good and some who are bad.
sentences.zh: 然而，任何一个民族的人，都会有好人，也有坏人。

sentences.en: This makes people very unlike wolves.
sentences.zh: 这使得人与狼非常不同。

sentences.en: Because some are good and some are bad, the best solution is to have an apparatus that detects the bad ones and deals with them in some way, such as deporting or imprisoning or fining them.
sentences.zh: 因为有些是好的，有些是坏的，所以最好的解决方案是有一个装置来检测坏的并以某种方式处理它们，例如驱逐出境或监禁或罚款。

sentences.en: It is not fair to punish them collectively for the crimes committed by only some of them.
sentences.zh: 仅因其中一些人犯下的罪行而对他们进行集体惩罚是不公平的。

sentences.en: You do not need to deport all of them to deport the ones who "take over public spaces".
sentences.zh: 你不需要驱逐所有“占领公共空间”的人。

sentences.en: Aside from fairness, are there other reasons to support individuated enforcement?
sentences.zh: 除了公平之外，还有其他理由支持个别执法吗？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Because almost all of the people involved are EU citizens, they cannot be deported without cause.
sentences.zh: 由于几乎所有涉案人员都是欧盟公民，他们不能无故被驱逐出境。

sentences.en: Any kind of mass deportation plan would have to change that, which would be legally tricky to say the least.
sentences.zh: 任何形式的大规模驱逐计划都必须改变这一点，至少可以说，这在法律上是很棘手的。

sentences.en: However, enforcing the existing laws requires no legal action, and could start tomorrow if the relevant executive wanted it to.
sentences.zh: 然而，执行现有法律不需要采取法律行动，如果相关行政人员愿意，可以从明天开始。

sentences.en: DHH might say "well, individuated enforcement sounds nice, but we don't seem to have the will to enforce our laws anymore."
sentences.zh: DHH 可能会说“嗯，个别执法听起来不错，但我们似乎不再愿意执行我们的法律。”

sentences.en: Well, my understanding of Denmark is that they also don't have the will to start doing mass deportations of EU citizens, and DHH is advocating to change that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对丹麦的理解是，他们也没有意愿开始大规模驱逐欧盟公民，而 DHH 正在倡导改变这一现状。

sentences.en: Why not advocate for individuated enforcement, seeing as it's the easier and fairer option? --- ## The Missing Mood Bryan Caplan has blogged about "[The Missing Moods](https://www.econlib.org/archives/2016/01/the_invisible_t.html)". He says: > You can learn a lot by comparing the mood reasonable proponents _would_ hold to the mood actual proponents _do_ hold.
sentences.zh: 既然这是更容易、更公平的选择，为什么不提倡单独执法呢？ --- ## 缺失的心情 布莱恩·卡普兰 (Bryan Caplan) 发表了有关“[缺失的心情](https://www.econlib.org/archives/2016/01/the_invisible_t.html)”的博客。他说： > 通过比较合理支持者_会_坚持的情绪和实际支持者_确实_坚持的情绪，你可以学到很多东西。

sentences.en: I think this concept is very instructive.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个概念非常有启发性。

sentences.en: He gives an example of a common "missing mood": > Modern warfare almost always leads to killing lots of innocents; if governments were held to the same standards as individuals, these killings would be manslaughter, if not murder.
sentences.zh: 他举了一个常见的“缺失情绪”的例子： > 现代战争几乎总是导致大量无辜者死亡；如果政府与个人遵循同样的标准，这些杀戮即使不是谋杀，也将是过失杀人。

sentences.en: This doesn’t mean that war is never justified.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着战争永远没有道理。

sentences.en: But the [reasonable hawkish mood](http://www.econlib.org/archives/2010/07/the_conservativ.html) is sorrow – and constant yearning for a peaceful path.
sentences.zh: 但[合理的鹰派情绪](http://www.econlib.org/archives/2010/07/the_conservativ.html)是悲伤——以及对和平道路的持续渴望。

sentences.en: The kind of emotions that flow out of, “We are in a tragic situation.
sentences.zh: 那种情感流露出来，“我们正处于悲惨的境地。

sentences.en: After painstaking research on all the available options, we regretfully conclude that we have to kill many thousands of innocent civilians in order to avoid even greater evils.
sentences.zh: 经过对所有可用选项的艰苦研究后，我们遗憾地得出结论：我们必须杀害成千上万的无辜平民，才能避免更大的罪恶。

sentences.en: This is true even after adjusting for the inaccuracy of our past predictions about foreign policy.” > > I have never personally known a hawk who expresses such moods, and know of none in the public eye.
sentences.zh: 即使在调整了我们过去对外交政策的预测的不准确性之后，情况也是如此。” >> 我个人从未见过有哪位鹰派会表达出这样的情绪，在公众眼中也没有这样的人。

sentences.en: Instead, the standard hawk moods are anger and machismo.
sentences.zh: 相反，标准的鹰派情绪是愤怒和大男子主义。

sentences.en: Ted Cruz’s [recent quip](http://www.bloomberg.com/politics/articles/2015-12-06/cruz-gaining-on-trump-in-iowa-intensifies-war-rhetoric), “I don’t know if sand can glow in the dark, but we’re going to find out” is typical.
sentences.zh: 特德·克鲁兹的[最近俏皮话](http://www.bloomberg.com/politics/articles/2015-12-06/cruz-gaining-on-trump-in-iowa-intensizes-war-rhetoric)，“我不知道沙子是否可以在黑暗中发光，但我们会发现”是典型的。

sentences.en: I think it's a good point.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个很好的观点。

sentences.en: War is often a terrible thing for civilians.
sentences.zh: 对于平民来说，战争往往是一件可怕的事情。

sentences.en: If initiating a war is truly necessary, then that's what you have to do, but it's odd to be happy about it.
sentences.zh: 如果确实有必要发动战争，那就必须这么做，但为此感到高兴就奇怪了。

sentences.en: And if you're happy about it, it gives others reason not to trust your reasoning.
sentences.zh: 如果你对此感到高兴，那么其他人就有理由不相信你的推理。

sentences.en: The same kind of applies here.
sentences.zh: 同样的情况也适用于此。

sentences.en: I think that the reasonable mood might be closer to "Romani people are simply causing more problems than our police force is equipped to handle right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为合理的情绪可能更接近于“罗姆人制造的问题比我们警察部队目前能够处理的问题还要多。

sentences.en: We have exhausted other options and for now the best option is to prevent new migration of Roma people into Denmark and gradually deport the ones we have.
sentences.zh: 我们已经用尽了其他选择，目前最好的选择是阻止新的罗姆人移民到丹麦，并逐步驱逐我们现有的罗姆人。

sentences.en: It's terrible that some innocent people who would have contributed to Denmark will be caught in the crossfire simply for being Romani, but there's simply no alternative."
sentences.zh: 一些本应为丹麦做出贡献的无辜者将仅仅因为是罗姆人而陷入交火，这是可怕的，但我们别无选择。”

sentences.en: But that's not the mood I got from the piece.
sentences.zh: 但这不是我从作品中得到的情绪。

sentences.en: That sentiment contains a factual error, that "there's simply no alternative".
sentences.zh: 这种观点包含一个事实错误，即“根本没有其他选择”。

sentences.en: As I mentioned earlier, the alternative is individuated enforcement.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，另一种选择是个别执法。

sentences.en: But my point is that it's possible to want what DHH wants while trying to treat everyone with dignity, and simply acknowledging an unfortunate reality where deportation of some innocent people is simply the best option.
sentences.zh: 但我的观点是，在努力有尊严地对待每个人的同时，我们有可能想要 DHH 想要的东西，并简单地承认一个不幸的现实，即驱逐一些无辜者只是最好的选择。

sentences.en: The fact that he isn't doing that suggests to me that there's a more fundamental mistake in his reasoning.
sentences.zh: 他没有这样做的事实向我表明，他的推理中存在一个更根本的错误。

sentences.en: Notice that in DHH's entire article, there's not a single sentence acknowledging that the category of "gypsy" contains uninvolved people contributing positively to Denmark.
sentences.zh: 请注意，在 DHH 的整篇文章中，没有一句话承认“吉普赛人”类别包含对丹麦做出积极贡献的无关人员。

sentences.en: I'd argue that every part of the post does the opposite.
sentences.zh: 我认为这篇文章的每个部分都做了相反的事情。

sentences.en: You should read the post to see for yourself, but it starts with a long section about the growing threat of wolves in Denmark.
sentences.zh: 您应该阅读这篇文章并亲自查看，但它首先用很长的一段内容介绍丹麦狼的威胁日益严重。

sentences.en: As I mentioned earlier, every wolf is a predator and a threat, and in Denmark according to DHH they are reproducing rapidly.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，每只狼都是捕食者和威胁，根据 DHH 的说法，在丹麦，它们的繁殖速度很快。

sentences.en: Immediately after, we have "Cue the gypsies in Copenhagen, and their increasingly brazen behavior".
sentences.zh: 紧接着，我们看到了“哥本哈根的吉普赛人，以及他们日益厚颜无耻的行为”。

sentences.en: There's no indication that there's any possibility that a single one could by innocent or worthy of respect, any more than there's an indication that a single wolf could be.
sentences.zh: 没有任何迹象表明一只狼可能是无辜的或值得尊重的，就像没有迹象表明一只狼可能是无辜的或值得尊重的一样。

sentences.en: Let's try to compare numerator to denominator.
sentences.zh: 让我们尝试比较分子和分母。

sentences.en: The "increasingly brazen behavior" that DHH constitutes "gypsies take\[ing] over public spaces", that must be stopped by "the basic logic of self-preservation," is one illegal tent camp.
sentences.zh: DHH 认为“吉普赛人占领公共场所”的“日益明目张胆的行为”必须以“自我保护的基本逻辑”来制止，这是一个非法帐篷营地。

sentences.en: I'd guess this constitutes tens of people.
sentences.zh: 我猜这有几十人。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, there are thousands of Roma living in Denmark. ------ Sunday, July 28, 2026
sentences.zh: 与此同时，有数千名罗姆人生活在丹麦。 ------ 2026 年 7 月 28 日星期日

content_html_zh: # 取消“Hey” 如果您不知道，“Hey”是一个颇受欢迎的电子邮件客户端，由行业传奇人物 DHH 创建。 我发现 Hey 非常适合我并且非常喜欢它。 它的费用是 99 美元/年，我已经成为忠实客户四年了，这意味着我总共给了他们 396 美元。 今天我发现1. 他们显然还有一个博客发布平台。 2. DHH 用它写了一篇题为“狼、羊和吉普赛人”的帖子(https://world.hey.com/dhh/wolves-sheep-and-gypsies-ba44af6a)。以下是其中的一段话： > 无论是狼还是吉普赛人，你都不能让问题失控。 你必须采取行动。 你必须保护羊。 当你的牲畜被掠食者吃掉，或者你的社区被移民占领时，你袖手旁观，这是对任何一个正常运转的社会对其公民最基本的义务的可悲的放弃。 > > 当狼失去控制时，你就射杀它们。 当吉普赛人占领公共场所时，你就将他们驱逐出境。 这并不难，也不残酷。 这是自我保护的基本逻辑。 我坚信“共存”。 这就是为什么我对DHH没有不好的感觉。 我绝对不相信通过对人们大喊大叫或羞辱他们来改变他们的想法。 我认为呐喊和羞耻的冲动来自“[冲突理论](https://slatestarcodex.com/2018/01/24/conflict-vs-mistake/)”，该理论说，当两个人出现政治分歧时，通常源于他们的价值观或利益冲突，而这种冲突永远无法友好解决。 我相信错误理论，该理论认为，当两个人存在政治分歧时，很可能他们都有共同的意图，但其中一个人在事实上是错误的。 我认为与事实错误的人断绝关系没有任何意义，因为这只会让我失去改变他们想法的能力。 但仍然有一条线。 我会成为你的朋友，但我不需要成为你的商业伙伴。 ---- Paul Graham [这样说](https://paulgraham.com/say.html): > 如果一个陈述是错误的，那是你能说的最糟糕的事情。 你不必说这是异端。 我喜欢这句话。 关注现实生活中的真假，而不是我们认为对手所做的陈述的关联和后果，是我们纠正错误的唯一方法。 然而，我不得不说，“如果一个陈述是错误的，那就是你能说的最糟糕的事情”这句话实际上是错误的。 例如，如果我给某人提供不准确的医疗建议，那不仅是错误的，而且是错误的和有害的。 而“虚假有害”比“虚假”更糟糕。 我想，如果我必须修改保罗·格雷厄姆的说法，我会说： > 错误的陈述只有在被相信的情况下才会造成伤害。 因此，要阻止该声明的危害，请让人们相信它是错误的。 我对措辞不太满意，但无论如何。 那么，DHH的哪项声明是错误的？ --- DHH 说： > 当狼失去控制时，你就射杀它们。 当吉普赛人占领公共场所时，你就将他们驱逐出境。 狼都是掠食者。 没有“好狼”（从羊的角度来看。） 因此，如果狼失去控制，有系统地射杀它们是有意义的。 然而，任何一个民族的人，都会有好人，也有坏人。 这使得人与狼非常不同。 因为有些是好的，有些是坏的，所以最好的解决方案是有一个装置来检测坏的并以某种方式处理它们，例如驱逐出境或监禁或罚款。 仅因其中一些人犯下的罪行而对他们进行集体惩罚是不公平的。 你不需要驱逐所有“占领公共空间”的人。 除了公平之外，还有其他理由支持个别执法吗？ 我想是的。 由于几乎所有涉案人员都是欧盟公民，他们不能无故被驱逐出境。 任何形式的大规模驱逐计划都必须改变这一点，至少可以说，这在法律上是很棘手的。 然而，执行现有法律不需要采取法律行动，如果相关行政人员愿意，可以从明天开始。 DHH 可能会说“嗯，个别执法听起来不错，但我们似乎不再愿意执行我们的法律。” 嗯，我对丹麦的理解是，他们也没有意愿开始大规模驱逐欧盟公民，而 DHH 正在倡导改变这一现状。 既然这是更容易、更公平的选择，为什么不提倡单独执法呢？ --- ## 缺失的心情 布莱恩·卡普兰 (Bryan Caplan) 发表了有关“[缺失的心情](https://www.econlib.org/archives/2016/01/the_invisible_t.html)”的博客。他说： > 通过比较合理支持者_会_坚持的情绪和实际支持者_确实_坚持的情绪，你可以学到很多东西。 我认为这个概念非常有启发性。 他举了一个常见的“缺失情绪”的例子： > 现代战争几乎总是导致大量无辜者死亡；如果政府与个人遵循同样的标准，这些杀戮即使不是谋杀，也将是过失杀人。 这并不意味着战争永远没有道理。 但[合理的鹰派情绪](http://www.econlib.org/archives/2010/07/the_conservativ.html)是悲伤——以及对和平道路的持续渴望。 那种情感流露出来，“我们正处于悲惨的境地。 经过对所有可用选项的艰苦研究后，我们遗憾地得出结论：我们必须杀害成千上万的无辜平民，才能避免更大的罪恶。 即使在调整了我们过去对外交政策的预测的不准确性之后，情况也是如此。” >> 我个人从未见过有哪位鹰派会表达出这样的情绪，在公众眼中也没有这样的人。 相反，标准的鹰派情绪是愤怒和大男子主义。 特德·克鲁兹的[最近俏皮话](http://www.bloomberg.com/politics/articles/2015-12-06/cruz-gaining-on-trump-in-iowa-intensizes-war-rhetoric)，“我不知道沙子是否可以在黑暗中发光，但我们会发现”是典型的。 我认为这是一个很好的观点。 对于平民来说，战争往往是一件可怕的事情。 如果确实有必要发动战争，那就必须这么做，但为此感到高兴就奇怪了。 如果你对此感到高兴，那么其他人就有理由不相信你的推理。 同样的情况也适用于此。 我认为合理的情绪可能更接近于“罗姆人制造的问题比我们警察部队目前能够处理的问题还要多。 我们已经用尽了其他选择，目前最好的选择是阻止新的罗姆人移民到丹麦，并逐步驱逐我们现有的罗姆人。 一些本应为丹麦做出贡献的无辜者将仅仅因为是罗姆人而陷入交火，这是可怕的，但我们别无选择。” 但这不是我从作品中得到的情绪。 这种观点包含一个事实错误，即“根本没有其他选择”。 正如我之前提到的，另一种选择是个别执法。 但我的观点是，在努力有尊严地对待每个人的同时，我们有可能想要 DHH 想要的东西，并简单地承认一个不幸的现实，即驱逐一些无辜者只是最好的选择。 他没有这样做的事实向我表明，他的推理中存在一个更根本的错误。 请注意，在 DHH 的整篇文章中，没有一句话承认“吉普赛人”类别包含对丹麦做出积极贡献的无关人员。 我认为这篇文章的每个部分都做了相反的事情。 您应该阅读这篇文章并亲自查看，但它首先用很长的一段内容介绍丹麦狼的威胁日益严重。 正如我之前提到的，每只狼都是捕食者和威胁，根据 DHH 的说法，在丹麦，它们的繁殖速度很快。 紧接着，我们看到了“哥本哈根的吉普赛人，以及他们日益厚颜无耻的行为”。 没有任何迹象表明一只狼可能是无辜的或值得尊重的，就像没有迹象表明一只狼可能是无辜的或值得尊重的一样。 让我们尝试比较分子和分母。 DHH 认为“吉普赛人占领公共场所”的“日益明目张胆的行为”必须以“自我保护的基本逻辑”来制止，这是一个非法帐篷营地。 我猜这有几十人。 与此同时，有数千名罗姆人生活在丹麦。 ------ 2026 年 7 月 28 日星期日
